newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds dip in dull market, no change seen.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds dip in dull market, no change seen.

text.p: Danish bond prices slipped moderately on Friday in a becalmed market ahead of April U.S. GDP data due at 1230 GMT.
"Only the U.S. GDP data can stir the market, which is falling on the French and German factors. It does not look like much is going to move today," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was down 0.14 point from the opening at 110.26, yielding 6.42 percent in 900 million crown turnover, while the forthcoming seven percent 2007 benchmark was 0.16 down at 102.76.

The 2007 paper's yield was at 6.61 percent in 500 million crown turnover. The June KFX future fell 0.02 point to 110.20 with 10 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.30 point to 88.95.
The crown traded at 3.8081 per mark at 1135 gmt, virtually the same as it started the day.
The 2006 benchmark's 10-year yield gap with Germany was unchanged at 47 basis points from the opening, with the 2007-bund differential at an unaltered 66 bps.
